newsitem.title: LATVIA: Foreigners buy into Latvian T-bills after rating.
newsitem.headline: Foreigners buy into Latvian T-bills after rating.

text.p: The investment grade credit rating which Latvia received last week produced its first results as the latest government T-bill issue was bought mostly by foreign banks and rates fell, the finance ministry said on Friday.
"One of the main reasons behind the continued fall (in rates) is the fact that foreign banks bought the majority of the paper," a finance ministry spokesman told a news conference.
"The credit rating has given its first results," he added.
The average weighted discount rate fell this week to 8.48 on Wednesday, he said. Yields on all the paper, which carried maturities of 28, 91 and 182 days, were below nine percent.
"Only two or three Latvian banks managed to buy something this time," the spokesman added.
Latvia was assigned an investment grade BBB for long-term currency debt and an A minus rating for long-term local currency debt by the U.S. Standard & Poors agency.

Latvia's is the second national credit rating in the Baltics but the first one of investment grade. Lithuania received a Ba2 grade from Moody's four months earlier, which classified it as distinctly speculative or of low creditworthiness.
